question: Which direction does a one-dimensional spectral JEPA learn when a fraction q of its positive pairs are two observations of one scene and the rest are two corruptions of one observation?

provenance.source: Balestriero and LeCun, arXiv:2610.39302v1: objective of Proposition 1 in its spectral contrastive form (Appendix A.1), product corruptions of Proposition 4(ii) and Theorem 5, good-view fraction q of Section 4.4
provenance.kind: authored from the equations of the paper; gradient flow of the population objective on a world of two scenes, each observed with two values of a nuisance

name: spectral JEPA with a fraction q of good views

carrier.name: amplitudes of the embedding on the world direction (w) and on the nuisance direction (u)

closure: gradient flow of the population objective; the noise of finite batches taken as additive
assumptions: finite world, uniform marginal, injective rendering of (scene, nuisance)
identity predictor, squared distance, second-order anti-collapse term in its soft (spectral contrastive) form
corruptions act on scene and nuisance independently
